This is a lesson on one comping rhythm the [Backing Track](../../tools/backing-track.qmd) band plays: **Strum: sixteenths**. It is built up from 2 simpler patterns, one step at a time, and every step is played by the band and written out as it plays. How the examples work: press ▶ Play, switch players in and out with the buttons beside it, and read what the band will play on the staff underneath: the whole pass is written out when Play starts, before it sounds. The tempo slider at the bottom of the page slows everything down.

[All the accompaniment patterns](index.qmd) · [Comping rhythms](index.qmd#chords)

## The pattern

The D, D-U, U-D-U strum at double speed, twice in the bar. For slow and medium tempos.

It belongs in *Acoustic strum*, *Straight-eighth rock* and *Dance pop*. Here it is in the acoustic strum style with the whole band. Switch the other players off to hear it alone.

<div class="ar-demo" data-style="strum" data-chart="C|G|Am|F" data-tempo="96" data-on="bass comp drums congas" data-staves="comp" data-comp="guitar" data-choice-label="Comping rhythm:" data-choices='[{"label":"Strum: sixteenths","opts":{"compRhythm":"strum16"}}]'></div>

## Step 1: Strum: down-up eighths

Start with something simpler. Every eighth note, down on the beat and up off it, leaning on 2 and 4.

This is a pattern of its own: [the lesson on it](chords-strum-eights.qmd) takes it further. Here it is only a step on the way, slowly. The drums keep time with you; switch the others on when it is steady.

<div class="ar-demo" data-style="strum" data-chart="C|G|Am|F" data-tempo="68" data-on="comp drums" data-staves="comp" data-comp="guitar" data-choice-label="Step:" data-choices='[{"label":"Strum: down-up eighths","opts":{"compRhythm":"strumEights"}}]'></div>

## Step 2: Strum: D, D-U, U-D-U

The strum most songbooks start with: down on 1, down-up on 2, then up, down-up through 3 and 4 (the hand misses the strings on beat 3).

This is a pattern of its own: [the lesson on it](chords-strum-camp.qmd) takes it further. Here it is only a step on the way, slowly. The drums keep time with you; switch the others on when it is steady.

<div class="ar-demo" data-style="strum" data-chart="C|G|Am|F" data-tempo="68" data-on="comp drums" data-staves="comp" data-comp="guitar" data-choice-label="Step:" data-choices='[{"label":"Strum: D, D-U, U-D-U","opts":{"compRhythm":"strumCamp"}}]'></div>

## Step 3: Strum: sixteenths, slowly

Now the pattern itself. Compare it with the step before: press each button while the band plays and watch what changes on the staff.

**How to play it.** The D, D-U, U-D-U strum twice as fast, twice a bar. The hand now moves down-up in sixteenths. Keep it small and from the wrist; start at half tempo.

<div class="ar-demo" data-style="strum" data-chart="C|G|Am|F" data-tempo="68" data-on="comp drums" data-staves="comp" data-comp="guitar" data-choice-label="Compare:" data-choices='[{"label":"Strum: sixteenths","opts":{"compRhythm":"strum16"}},{"label":"Strum: D, D-U, U-D-U (the step before)","opts":{"compRhythm":"strumCamp"}}]'></div>

## Step 4: Up to tempo, with the band

The whole band, at 96 beats a minute. Play along, then switch the band's chord player off and take the part yourself.

<div class="ar-demo" data-style="strum" data-chart="C|G|Am|F" data-tempo="96" data-on="bass comp drums congas" data-staves="comp bass" data-comp="guitar" data-choice-label="Comping rhythm:" data-choices='[{"label":"Strum: sixteenths","opts":{"compRhythm":"strum16"}}]'></div>

## Step 5: Two chords in a bar

Harder: now some bars have two chords, two beats each. The pattern keeps its rhythm and changes chord where the bar does: watch the staff for the hit that lands on beat 3.

<div class="ar-demo" data-style="strum" data-chart="C G|Am F|C G|F G" data-tempo="96" data-on="bass comp drums congas" data-staves="comp bass" data-comp="guitar" data-choice-label="Comping rhythm:" data-choices='[{"label":"Strum: sixteenths","opts":{"compRhythm":"strum16"}}]'></div>
